headline_marked: Mbappe says France [[happy to get hands dirty]] to win World Cup
headline: Mbappe says France happy to get hands dirty to win World Cup
summary: France captain Kylian Mbappe says his team is ready to play 'dirty' if necessary to advance, following a gritty 1-0 win over Paraguay.
details: France captain Kylian Mbappe stated that his side is willing to do whatever it takes to advance in the World Cup after a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Paraguay on Saturday.
Mbappe scored the winning goal from a penalty in the 70th minute, bringing his tournament total to seven goals and his overall World Cup tally to 19.
The match in Philadelphia was described as a 'scrappy affair' with players from both sides squaring off, including Paraguayan defenders attempting to disrupt the penalty spot.
Mbappe commented that while France is known for attacking football, they are not just a team that plays spectacular moves and are capable of playing the 'dirty game' to win.
The match ended with three yellow cards, all of which were given to French players by Uzbek referee Ilgiz Tantashev.
France will now face Morocco in the quarterfinals next Friday in Boston, a repeat of the 2022 semifinal where France won 2-0.
caption:
“We know how to play the dirty game too.”

France captain Kylian Mbappe stated that his side is willing to do whatever it takes to advance in the World Cup after a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Paraguay on Saturday.

Mbappe scored the winning goal from a penalty in the 70th minute, bringing his tournament total to seven goals and his overall World Cup tally to 19.

The match in Philadelphia was described as a 'scrappy affair' with players from both sides squaring off, including Paraguayan defenders attempting to disrupt the penalty spot.

Mbappe commented that while France is known for attacking football, they are not just a team that plays spectacular moves and are capable of playing the 'dirty game' to win.

The match ended with three yellow cards, all of which were given to French players by Uzbek referee Ilgiz Tantashev.

France will now face Morocco in the quarterfinals next Friday in Boston, a repeat of the 2022 semifinal where France won 2-0.
